newsitem.title: ITALY: WFP launches major feeding programme in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: WFP launches major feeding programme in Zaire.

text.p: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) said on Monday that it was launching a massive feeding programme for refugees in the Goma region of eastern Zaire to reduce the threat of looting of supplies.
WFP spokesman Trevor Rowe said the cost of food in the area had shot up because of fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops and there were fears that looters might target the WFP's supplies.

"In order to avoid looting -- and there have already been some incidents where people have indicated they might want to loot one of our warehouses -- we are going to launch a massive, massive feeding programme," Rowe told Reuters Television.
He said the programme would reach roughly 680,000 people in the region with WFP providing the food and various non-governmental organisations (NGOs) distributing it.
"This will provide a ration of about one week per person," Rome said.
A line of refugee camps from Goma to Bukavu stretches over 250 km (160 miles) in the extreme east of Zaire facing both Rwanda and Burundi.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has estimated that 500,000 people -- most of them Rwandan and Burundian refugees -- have been uprooted by more than a week of fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops.
Rowe said much depended on security conditions, on transport and on whether refugees crossed back into Rwanda.

A group of foreigners left Bukavu earlier on Monday in a road convoy escorted by Zairean troops to be evacuated by plane, witnesses said. Most foreign aid workers left the town on Saturday because of worsening security.
